translation.title: Smoking Cessation Aid Adhesive Patch
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used as an aid to smoking cessation.
translation.usage: Adults apply one patch once a day to a hairless part of the body (such as the buttock or the inner arm), changing the application site every day. Nicostop-30 is generally used by people who smoke 20 or more cigarettes a day, and Nicostop-20 by people who smoke up to 20 cigarettes a day. Nicostop-10 is used in the final stage to reduce nicotine replacement. Heavy smokers start with Nicostop-30, then move to Nicostop-20 and finally to Nicostop-10, using each for 4 weeks. Average smokers use Nicostop-20 for 8 weeks and then Nicostop-10 for 4 weeks. Treatment must not exceed 3 months.
translation.caution: If you keep smoking while using this medicine, nicotine can cause cardiovascular side effects more often and more markedly, so only people who have stopped smoking completely should use it. Do not use this medicine in the following cases: people who are hypersensitive to this medicine; chronic skin disease (psoriasis, chronic dermatitis, urticaria); generalised skin disease; hypersensitivity dermatitis; unstable angina; worsening angina; people who have had a myocardial infarction within the past 3 months; the late phase of acute infarction; severe cardiac arrhythmia; systemic hypertension; peripheral vascular disease; people with cerebrovascular disease (acute stroke, cerebrovascular abnormality); pregnant or breastfeeding women; children and adolescents under 18 years of age; non-smokers and occasional smokers. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before using this medicine in the following cases: elderly people; gastritis; acute gastric ulcer; occlusive arterial disease; stable angina; heart failure; decompensated heart failure; myocardial infarction; cardiac arrhythmia; vasospasm; uncontrolled hypertension; people who have had arterial bypass grafting or angioplasty; renal failure; hepatic failure; diabetes; hyperthyroidism; people with phaeochromocytoma. Do not use several patches at the same time. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you use it together with any of the following: paracetamol; caffeine; imipramine; oxazepam; pentazocine; propranolol; theophylline; warfarin; oestrogen; lignocaine; phenacetin; insulin; adrenergic antagonists (such as prazosin and labetalol); flecainide; adrenergic agonists (such as isoprenaline and phenylephrine); propoxyphene; theophylline; tacrine; clozapine; ropinirole. Stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist if any of the following occur: erythema; swelling; allergy; skin eruption; herpetiform eruption; itching; urticaria; acne; skin discolouration (rarely). The following may occur: headache; dizziness; sleep disturbance; anxiety; emotional instability; restlessness; abnormal dreams; somnolence; agitation; impaired concentration; fatigue; migraine; spasms; leg cramps; changes in blood pressure; high blood pressure; palpitations; nausea; abdominal pain; indigestion; constipation; diarrhoea; vomiting; gastric ulcer; difficulty swallowing; abnormal bowel movements; increased appetite; cold and influenza symptoms; cough; pharyngitis; rhinitis; sinusitis; upper respiratory symptoms; bronchitis; difficulty breathing; taste disturbance; visual disturbance; dysmenorrhoea; muscle pain; joint pain; toothache; back pain; chest pain; pain; earache; facial flushing; localised swelling; weight gain; dry mouth; flatulence; gingivitis; thyroid dysfunction; lymph node pain; cystitis; increased sweating. Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light. Keep out of reach of children.
